SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl came upon the Prophet praying and forbade him, prompting the passage about the one who forbids a servant when he prays through the sinful, lying forelock.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي فجاءه أبو جهل فنهاه فأنزل الله ﴿ أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى ﴾

BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r1.claim: The question expresses amazement; seeing is visual, the address reaches anyone capable of seeing, and the indefinite servant magnifies Muhammad’s perfect servanthood.
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r1.anchor: الاستفهام للتعجيب والرؤية بصرية والخطاب لكل من

BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r2.claim: Saying that the man forbids a servant from praying, rather than saying he forbids you, stresses the servant’s worship of his Master and the ugliness of obstructing it.
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r2.anchor: والعدول عن ينهاك إلى ينهى عبدا دال على أن النهي كان للعبد عن إقامة خدمة مولاه ولا أقبح منه

BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r3.speaker: أبو جهل
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r3.claim: Abu Jahl threatened in a Quraysh gathering to trample Muhammad’s neck if he saw him praying.
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r3.anchor: روى أن أبا جهل قال في ملأ من طغاة قريش لئن رأيت محمدا يصلى لأطأن عنقه

BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r4.claim: A report in al-Takmila says Abu Jahl approached Muhammad at noon prayer intending to drop a stone on him, then retreated after seeing a fiery trench and angels’ wings.
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r4.anchor: على رأسه حجرا فرآه في الصلاة وهي صلاة الظهر فجاءه ثم نكص على عقبيه

BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r5.claim: Abu Jahl saw the angels’ wings but not their persons; Muhammad swore that the angels would have torn him limb from limb had he approached.
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r5.anchor: والمراد أجنحة الملائكة أبصر اللعين الأجنحة ولم يبصر أصحابها فقال عليه السلام ، والذي نفسي بيده لو دنا مني لاختطفته الملائكة عضوا عضوا

BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r6.claim: Abu Jahl had been nicknamed Abu al-Hakam in paganism because people deemed him wise, but Islam named him Abu Jahl.
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r6.anchor: وكان أبو جهل يكنى في الجاهلية بأبي الحكم لأنهم كانوا يزعمون أنه عالم ذو حكمة ثم سمى أبا جهل في الإسلام.

BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r7.claim: The Prophet prayed for Islam to be strengthened through Abu Jahl or Umar; Umar’s conversion showed him the happiest Qurayshi, just as Abu Jahl was the most wretched, since opposites reveal one another.
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r7.anchor: يدعو ويقول اللهم أعز الإسلام بأبي جهل أو بعمر فلما أعزه الله بعمر رضي الله عنه دل على أن عمر أسعد قريش كما أن أبا

BURSEVI:v10p366/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366/r1.speaker: أبو الليث
BURSEVI:v10p366/r1.claim: Abu al-Layth says the verse admonishes everyone and threatens anyone who prevents good and obedience.
BURSEVI:v10p366/r1.anchor: قال أبو الليث رحمه الله : والآية عظة لجميع الناس وتهديد لمن يمنع عن الخير وعن الطاعة

BURSEVI:v10p366/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366/r2.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v10p366/r2.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says that although revealed about Abu Jahl, anyone who forbids obedience shares his threat.
BURSEVI:v10p366/r2.anchor: وقال ابن الشيخ في حواشيه وهذه الآية وإن نزلت في حق أبي جهل لكن كل من نهى عن طاعة فهو شريك أبي جهل في هذا

BURSEVI:v10p366/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366/r3.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v10p366/r3.claim: A prohibition of praying in a usurped place or at a disliked time concerns the accompanying sin, not prayer itself; an invalid attribute does not invalidate the underlying prayer.
BURSEVI:v10p366/r3.anchor: ولا يلم عليه المنع من الصلاة في الدار المغصوبة والأوقات المكروهة لأن المنهي عنه غير الصلاة وهو المعصية

BURSEVI:v10p366/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366/r4.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v10p366/r4.claim: Because forbidding an accompanying attribute can sound like forbidding prayer itself, some authorities avoided an explicit prohibition out of caution.
BURSEVI:v10p366/r4.anchor: بينهما بحيث يكون النهي عن الوصف موهما للنهي عن الأصل احتاط فيه بعض الأكابر

BURSEVI:v10p366/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366/r5.speaker: علي
BURSEVI:v10p366/r5.claim: Ali saw people praying before the Eid prayer and said he had not seen the Prophet do so; when asked whether to forbid them, he feared falling under the threat and stayed indirect.
BURSEVI:v10p366/r5.anchor: روى عن علي رضي الله عنه ، إنه رأى في المصلى أقواما يصلون قبل صلاة العيد فقال : ما رأيت رسول الله

BURSEVI:v10p366/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BURSEVI:v10p366/r6.claim: Abu Hanifa followed this caution: when Abu Yusuf asked about saying a forgiveness prayer after bowing, he directed him to say “Our Lord, praise is Yours” and prostrate without explicitly forbidding it.
BURSEVI:v10p366/r6.anchor: حتى قال له أبو يوسف أيقول المصلى حين يرفع رأسه من الركوع اللهم اغفر لي قال يقول ربنا لك الحمد ويسجد ولم يصرح بالنهي

BURSEVI:v10p366/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366/r7.claim: Kalla rebukes and disgraces the tyrant who forbids worship of God and urges worship of al-Lāt.
BURSEVI:v10p366/r7.anchor: كلا} ردع للناهي اللعين وخسو له عن نهيه عن عبادة الله وأمره بعبادة اللات

QASHANI:96:9-14/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:96:9-14/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:96:9-14/r1.claim: The one who forbids is a veiled, ignorant person self-satisfied with his condition, wealth, and clan; the servant is one who prays in attentive presence and worshipful steadiness, whom the forbidding man opposes.
QASHANI:96:9-14/r1.anchor: المحجوب الجاهل المستغني بحاله وماله وقومه عن الحق

QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r11.claim: The rebuke of the one who forbids a servant from praying implies that it would have been better for him not to do so.
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r11.anchor: ينهى عبدا إذا صلى } . أليس لو لم يفعل هذا كان خيرا له ؟ ففي الآية هذا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#3/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the one who forbids prayer as Abu Jahl, the 'assembly' as his clan, and the summoned wardens as angels.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ارايت الذي ينهى عبدا اذا صلى قال : أبو جهل نهى محمدا اذا صلى فليدع نادية قال : عشيرته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r7.claim: Kalla is a rebuke and invalidation; appearing before any obvious target indicates that the intended target follows, namely the one who forbids a servant from praying.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r1.claim: Kalla normally follows the speech it rejects, but here it opens the sentence because the following statement is what deserves repudiation; Imru al-Qays offers a similar initial negative particle.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r1.anchor: وحق { كلا } أن تقع بعد كلام لإبطاله والزجر عن مضمونه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r2.claim: Muslim transmits Abu Jahl's threat to trample Muhammad's neck while praying; when he approached, he recoiled from a fiery trench and terror, and the Prophet said angels would have torn him apart. The report is linked to revelation of these verses, though its placement in Abu Hurayra's report is uncertain.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r2.anchor: روى مسلم عن أبي حازم عن أبي هريرة قال : ( قال أبو جهل : هل يعفر محمد وجهه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r3.speaker: الطبري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r3.claim: Al-Tabari says the verses beginning 'Have you seen the one who forbids' descended about Abu Jahl's threat to trample Muhammad during prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r3.anchor: وقال الطبري : ذكر أن آية { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى } وما بعدها نزلت في أبي جهل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r4.claim: The accounts can be reconciled: the passage beginning at 96:9 directly concerns Abu Jahl, while the statement about human transgression through 96:8 prepares for it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r4.anchor: ووجه الجمع بين الروايتين : أن النازل في أبي جهل بعضه مقصود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r5.claim: Exegetes disagree whether these verses followed the first five immediately; prayer's mention seems problematic if obligatory prayer began at the Night Journey years later. Some posit intervening revelation and later attachment, while others deny this was the first revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r5.anchor: واختلفوا في أن هذه الآيات إلى آخر السورة نزلت عقب الخمس الآيات الماضية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r1.claim: Exegetes agree that the one who forbids the worshipper is Abu Jahl, who threatened to trample Muhammad’s neck if he saw him praying at the Kaaba; this was a threat meant to reach Muhammad, not a face-to-face prohibition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r1.anchor: اتفقوا على أنه أريد به أبو جهل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r4.claim: The address may also describe visual witnessing of an actual event; the addressee of the question is unspecified.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الرؤية بصرية لأنها حكاية أمر وقع في الخارج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r5.claim: “A servant” refers to the Prophet but deliberately generalizes him as any person devoted to God, making the prohibition itself astonishing regardless of the worshipper’s identity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r5.anchor: والمراد بالعبد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وإطلاق العبد هنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r6.claim: The present tense pictures the extraordinary scene vividly although Abu Jahl’s prohibition had already occurred, and the omitted prohibited act is understood from the prayer context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r6.anchor: لاستحضار الحالة العجيبة وإلا فإن نهيه قد مضى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#7/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#7/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#7/r3.claim: Abu Huraira reports Abu Jahl's threat to step on Muhammad's neck while he prayed; when he approached, he recoiled, describing a trench of fire, terror and wings, and the Prophet said angels would have seized him limb by limb.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#7/r3.anchor: قال أبو هريرة قال أبو جهل هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#7/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#7/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#7/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl confronted the Prophet in prayer; after the Prophet rebuked him, Abu Jahl boasted of his clan, prompting the warning to call his assembly and the promise of the guards of Hell.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#7/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي فجاء أبو جهل فقال ألم أنهك عن هذا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#7/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#7/r5.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#7/r5.claim: The servant being prayed against is Muhammad; some say the prayer was the noon prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#7/r5.anchor: قال المفسرون والمراد بالعبد هاهنا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وقيل كانت الصلاة صلاة الظهر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r4.claim: The one who forbids prayer is Abu Jahl, who threatened Muhammad for praying at the Kaaba; God first rebukes him by asking what he thinks if the worshipper follows guidance or commands piety.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r4.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل، لعنه الله، توعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على الصلاة عند البيت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports Abu Jahl swearing to trample Muhammad while he prayed; as he approached he recoiled, describing a trench of fire, terror, and wings. The Prophet says angels would have snatched him limb by limb; the narrator is unsure whether the revelation context was part of Abu Hurayra's report. Ibn Kathir says Ahmad, Muslim, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Abi Hatim transmit it through Mu'tamir.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال أبو جهل: هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم؟ قالوا: نعم. قال: فقال: واللات والعزى لئن رأيته يصلي

FARRA:v3p278/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p278/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p278/r5.claim: The passage was revealed about Abū Jahl, who came to the Prophet’s prayer place, harmed him, and tried to stop him praying.
FARRA:v3p278/r5.anchor:
عبدا إذا صلى، (10) .
نزلت في أبي جهل: كان يأتي رسول الله

JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r1.claim: Ending means refraining from an act.
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r1.anchor: الانتهاء: الامتناع من الفعل، انتهى انتهاء.

JISHUMI:v10p7481/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r4.claim: The passage was revealed about Abū Jahl forbidding the Prophet to pray.
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r4.anchor: قيل: نزلت الآيات في أبي جهل بن هشام لعنه الله لما نهى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم وآله - عن الصلاة، عن ابن عباس، وقتادة.

JISHUMI:v10p7481/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r5.claim: Abū Jahl threatened to trample Muḥammad's neck if he prayed; when he saw him praying, he fled and said a trench of fire lay between them.
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r5.anchor: قال: لئن فعل ذلك لأطأن عنقه، قالوا: ها هو ذاك يصلي، فانطلق ثم أدبر هاربا، فقالوا: ما لك؟

JISHUMI:v10p7481/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r8.speaker: أبو جهل
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r8.claim: One view identifies the forbidding person as Abū Jahl, while another makes the warning general; the mention of forbidding is rebuke and threat, or astonishment mixed with warning.
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r8.anchor: قيل: هو أبو جهل نهى النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم -، وذكر النهي وأراد به التهديد والتقريع،

JISHUMI:v10p7482/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r6.claim: Forbidding prayer, obedience, or guidance is reprehensible, and the verse supports the duty to enjoin right and forbid wrong.
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r6.anchor: يدل قوله: (أرأيت الذي ينهى) على قبح النهي عن الصلاة، وعن كل طاعة وهدى

KASHSHAF:96:9/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:9/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:9/r1.claim: The question means: tell me about the person who stops a servant of God from praying.
KASHSHAF:96:9/r1.anchor: ومعناه : أخبرني عمن ينهى بعض عباد الله عن صلاته

KASHSHAF:96:10/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:10/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:10/r1.claim: The question means: tell me about the person who stops a servant of God from praying.
KASHSHAF:96:10/r1.anchor: ومعناه : أخبرني عمن ينهى بعض عباد الله عن صلاته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r8.speaker: أبو جهل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r8.claim: Abu Jahl threatened to trample the Prophet's neck if he saw him praying, but recoiled and described a trench of fire and wings between them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r8.anchor: فوالذي يحلف به ، لئن رأيته توطأت عنقه

MUQATIL:96:9-19/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r1.claim: When prayer was prescribed for Muhammad in Mecca, Abū Jahl threatened to cut off his head if he saw him praying; the verse's man who forbids a servant from prayer is the Prophet.
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r1.anchor: فرضت عليه الصلاة بمكة، فقال أبو جهل: لئن رأيت محمدا يصلى لأضربن عنقه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#4/r1.claim: The person who forbids a servant from praying is Abu Jahl attempting to stop Muhammad from prayer.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#4/r1.anchor: أى أرأيت أبا جهل ينهى محمدا عن الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:96:9-10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:9-10/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:9-10/r1.claim: The one who forbids prayer is Abu Jahl and the worshipping servant is Muhammad; Abu Jahl threatened to trample the Prophet's neck if he saw him praying, prompting these verses in astonishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:9-10/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { أرأيت الذي ينهى } وهو أبو جهل { عبدا } وهو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:9-10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:9-10/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:96:9-10/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra is the authority for Abu Jahl's threat to step on Muhammad's neck if he saw him praying.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:9-10/r2.anchor: قاله أبو هريرة. فأنزل الله هذه الآيات تعجبا منه.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:9-10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:9-10/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:9-10/r3.claim: The wording contains an ellipsis, asking whether this forbidding man is safe from punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:9-10/r3.anchor: وقيل: في الكلام حذف والمعنى: أمن هذا الناهي عن الصلاة من العقوبة.

QUTB-ZILAL:96:9/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:9/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:9/r2.claim: Its denunciation and wonder are conveyed through a distinctive live-address style of quick, broken touches, difficult to reproduce in writing.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:9/r2.anchor: والتشنيع والتعجيب واضح في طريقة التعبير ،  التي تتعذر مجاراتها في لغة الكتابة

QUTB-ZILAL:96:10/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:10/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:10/r1.claim: The repeated question makes listeners witness the scandalous act, then intensifies it by adding one ugliness and brutality to another.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:10/r1.anchor: أرأيت حين تضم شناعة إلى شناعة ? وتضاف بشاعة إلى بشاعة ?

QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r2.speaker: الروايات الصحيحة
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r2.claim: Sound reports say all but the surah's opening passage was revealed about Abu Jahl after he saw Muhammad praying at the Maqam and forbade him.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r2.anchor: وردت بعض الروايات الصحيحة بأن السورة - عدا المقطع الأول منها - قد نزلت في أبي جهل

RAZI:96:10/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:10/r1.speaker: أبو جهل
RAZI:96:10/r1.claim: Abū Jahl threatened to trample the Prophet’s neck if he saw him praying, but when he did, he recoiled, saying a fiery trench and terrible barrier lay between them.
RAZI:96:10/r1.anchor: أنه قال : هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم ؟ قالوا : نعم

RAZI:96:10/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:10/r2.speaker: الحسن
RAZI:96:10/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says Umayya ibn Khalaf used to prevent Salmān from praying.
RAZI:96:10/r2.anchor: وعن الحسن أن أمية بن خلف كان ينهى سلمان عن الصلاة

RAZI:96:10/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:10/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:96:10/r3.claim: The verse appears to concern the previously mentioned person, hence reports that it was revealed about Abū Jahl; a specific occasion can still have general application, though what follows points to a particular man.
RAZI:96:10/r3.anchor: ظاهر الآية أن المراد في هذه الآية هو الإنسان المتقدم ذكره

RAZI:96:10/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:10/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:96:10/r4.claim: “Have you seen?” addresses the Prophet in astonishment: he had prayed for Islam to be strengthened through Abū Jahl or ʿUmar, yet Abū Jahl forbids prayer.
RAZI:96:10/r4.anchor: اللهم أعز الإسلام إما بأبي جهل بن هشام أو بعمر

RAZI:96:10/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:10/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:96:10/r5.claim: Abū Jahl was called Abū al-Ḥakam, so it is astonishing to call him wise while he stops worship of God and bows to idols.
RAZI:96:10/r5.anchor: أنه كان يلقب بأبي الحكم ، فكأنه تعالى يقول : كيف يليق به هذا اللقب

RAZI:96:10/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:10/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:96:10/r6.claim: The fool commands others as though he deserves obedience although he is neither creator nor lord, yet forbids obedience to the true Lord and Creator.
RAZI:96:10/r6.anchor: ذلك الأحمق يأمر وينهى ، ويعتقد أنه يجب على الغير طاعته

RAZI:96:10/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:10/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:96:10/r7.claim: The indefinite “a servant” signals complete devotion; an account has a learned Jew ask ʿAlī about the Prophet’s character, and ʿAlī argues that it exceeds description just as the world does, citing scripture.
RAZI:96:10/r7.anchor: أن التنكير في عبدا يدل على كونه كاملا في العبودية

RAZI:96:10/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:10/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:96:10/r8.claim: The indefinite form also heightens blame by describing the forbidding as the man’s regular habit toward anyone he sees.
RAZI:96:10/r8.anchor: أن هذا أبلغ في الذم لأن المعنى أن هذا دأبه وعادته فينهى كل من يرى

RAZI:96:10/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:10/r9.speaker: علي
RAZI:96:10/r9.claim: ʿAlī saw people praying before the Eid prayer and did not stop them because he feared falling under the verse’s warning against forbidding a worshipper.
RAZI:96:10/r9.anchor: روي عن علي عليه السلام أنه رأى في المصلى أقواما يصلون قبل صلاة العيد

RAZI:96:10/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:10/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI:96:10/r10.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa adopted this restraint: when Abū Yūsuf asked whether a worshipper should say “God forgive me” after bowing, he prescribed the regular praise and prostration without explicitly forbidding it.
RAZI:96:10/r10.anchor: وأخذ أبو حنيفة منه هذا الأدب الجميل حيث قال له أبو يوسف

RAZI:96:10/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:10/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:96:10/r11.claim: The verse also rebukes Abū Jahl for thinking that if Muḥammad did not prostrate, no one else would: countless nearby angels continually pray and glorify God.
RAZI:96:10/r11.anchor: أيظن أبو جهل أنه لو لم يسجد محمد لي لا أجد ساجدا غيره

RAZI:96:10/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:10/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:96:10/r12.claim: The indefinite servant magnifies the Prophet: although grammatically indefinite, he is uniquely identifiable, as in Qurʾanic references to God’s servant.
RAZI:96:10/r12.anchor: أنه تفخيم لشأن النبي عليه السلام يقول : إنه مع التنكير معرف

TAB:96:9/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:9/r1.speaker: author
TAB:96:9/r1.claim: The passage was revealed about Abu Jahl, who threatened to trample Muhammad's neck and forbade him to pray at the Maqam; God highlights his bold ignorance and rejection despite God's favors.
TAB:96:9/r1.anchor: ذُكر أن هذه الاَية وما بعدها نزلت في أبي جهل بن هشام ،   وذلك أنه قال فيما بلغنا

TAB:96:9/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:9/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:96:9/r2.claim: Mujahid identifies the one who forbids a servant to pray as Abu Jahl forbidding Muhammad.
TAB:96:9/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   في قول الله :  {  أرأَيْتَ الّذِي يَنْهَى عَبْدا إذَا صَلّى } قال :  أبو جهل ،   يَنْهَى محمدا

TAB:96:9/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:9/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB:96:9/r3.claim: Qatada says Abu Jahl threatened to step on Muhammad's neck if he saw him praying, prompting the revelation.
TAB:96:9/r3.anchor: عن قتادة {  أرأيْتَ الّذِي يَنْهَى عَبْدا إذَا صَلّى } نزلت في عدوّ الله أبي جهل ،   وذلك لأنه قال

TAB:96:9/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:9/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB:96:9/r4.claim: Qatada also reports the saying that every nation has a Pharaoh, and this community's Pharaoh is Abu Jahl.
TAB:96:9/r4.anchor: عن قتادة ،   في قول الله :  {  أرأَيْتَ الّذِي يَنْهَى عَبْدا إذَا صَلّى } قال :  قال أبو جهل

TAB:96:9/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:9/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:96:9/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Abu Jahl came upon Muhammad praying, forbade him, and the passage through ‘lying and sinning’ was revealed.
TAB:96:9/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قال :  كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلّي ،   فجاءه أبو جهل

TAB:96:14/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:14/r2.speaker: author
TAB:96:14/r2.claim: The three repetitions of araʾayta work by substitution; the sense is whether the forbidding, denying man knows that God sees him.
TAB:96:14/r2.anchor: أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى ،   أرأيت إن كان على الهدى } ،   فكررت أرأيت مرات ثلاثا على البدل

TAB-FULL:v24p533#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p533#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p533#2/r1.claim: Al-Tabari addresses Muhammad about Abu Jahl at the prayer place, emphasizing his denial of truth and audacity.
TAB-FULL:v24p533#2/r1.anchor: أرأيت يا محمد أبا جهل الذي ينهاك أن تصلي عند المقام، وهو معرض عن الحق، مكذب به،

TAB-FULL:v24p533#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p533#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p533#2/r2.claim: Mujahid identifies Abu Jahl as the man who forbade Muhammad from praying.
TAB-FULL:v24p533#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد،. في قول الله: {أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى} [العلق: 10] قال: أبو جهل، ينهى محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا صلى

TAB-FULL:v24p533#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p533#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p533#2/r3.claim: Qatada says the verse was revealed about Abu Jahl, who threatened to trample Muhammad’s neck if he saw him praying.
TAB-FULL:v24p533#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى} [العلق: 10] نزلت في عدو الله أبي جهل، وذلك لأنه قال: لئن رأيت محمدا يصلي لأطأن على عنقه

TAB-FULL:v24p533#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p533#2/r4.speaker: قائل غير مسمى
TAB-FULL:v24p533#2/r4.claim: Qatada also reports the saying that every nation has a Pharaoh and Abu Jahl was this community’s Pharaoh.
TAB-FULL:v24p533#2/r4.anchor: «لكل أمة فرعون، وفرعون هذه الأمة أبو جهل»

TAB-FULL:v24p533#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p533#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p533#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl stopped the Prophet while he prayed, prompting revelation through the description of the lying, sinful forelock.
TAB-FULL:v24p533#2/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، قال: كان رسول صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي، فجاءه أبو جهل، فنهاه أن يصلي

TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports Abu Jahl’s threat, his sudden retreat from a trench of fire, awe and wings, and the Prophet’s statement that angels would tear him apart; the passage gives the revealed sequence.
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: قال أبو جهل: هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم؟ قال: فقيل: نعم، قال: فقال: واللات والعزى لئن رأيته

TAB-FULL:v24p539/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abu Jahl threatened to kill Muhammad at the prayer place; when Muhammad prayed, Abu Jahl saw dark battalions between them and would have been seized by angels.
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r2.anchor: عن الوليد بن العيزار، عن ابن عباس، قال: قال أبو جهل: لئن عاد محمد يصلي عند المقام لأقتلنه، فأنزل الله:

TAB-FULL:v24p539/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Abu Jahl’s vow to trample the Prophet’s neck and the Prophet’s warning that angels would seize him visibly.
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r3.anchor: عن عبد الكريم، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، قال: قال أبو جهل: لئن رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي عند الكعبة، لآتينه

ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r3.claim: These verses were revealed concerning Abū Jahl ibn Hishām, who threatened to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him praying.
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r3.anchor:
هذه نزلت في أبي جهل بن هشام، وكذلك: (أرأيت الذي ينهى (9) عبدا إذا صلى (10).
لأن أبا جهل قال: إن رأيت محمدا يصلي توطأت عنقه.

THALABI:v10p246/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p246/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p246/r2.claim: The passage about the one who forbids prayer was revealed concerning Abū Jahl, who tried to stop the Prophet praying.
THALABI:v10p246/r2.anchor: أرأيت الذي ينهى. عبدا إذا صلى نزلت في أبي جهل- لعنه الله- نهى النبي

THALABI:v10p246/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p246/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v10p246/r3.claim: He reports Abū Jahl’s threat to trample Muḥammad’s neck, followed by Abū Jahl recoiling and describing a trench of fire, horror, and wings between them.
THALABI:v10p246/r3.anchor:
هريرة قال: قال أبو جهل: هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم؟
قالوا: نعم، قال: فو الذي يحلف به لئن رأيته

THALABI:v10p246/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p246/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p246/r4.claim: The Prophet says that if Abū Jahl had approached him, angels would have seized him limb by limb.
THALABI:v10p246/r4.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: لو دنا مني لاختطفته الملائكة عضوا عضوا

THALABI:v10p246/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p246/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p246/r6.claim: When Abū Jahl forbade prayer and was rebuked, he threatened to summon cavalry or footmen; the Prophet said the guards would take him openly.
THALABI:v10p246/r6.anchor: لأملأن عليك إن شئت هذا خيلا جردا أو رجالا مردا، فأنزل الله سبحانه فليدع ناديه أي قومه

ASAD-NOTES:96:9#n5/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:96:9#n5/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:96:9#n5/r1.claim: The wording suggests an attempt to prevent prayer; classical commentators identify Abu Jahl's efforts to stop Muhammad and followers praying publicly at the Ka'bah, in a passage revealed at least a year after 96:1–5.
ASAD-NOTES:96:9#n5/r1.anchor: most of the classical commentators see in this passage (which was revealed at least a year later than the first five verses)

ASAD-NOTES:96:9#n5/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:96:9#n5/r2.speaker: classical commentators
ASAD-NOTES:96:9#n5/r2.claim: They read the passage historically as referring to Abu Jahl's attempts to stop Muhammad and his followers praying at the Ka'bah.
ASAD-NOTES:96:9#n5/r2.anchor: an allusion to Abu Jahl, the Prophet's bitterest opponent in Mecca

ASAD-NOTES:96:9#n5/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:96:9#n5/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:96:9#n5/r3.claim: Asad says the passage applies beyond that incident to all efforts to exclude religion from shaping social life, whether by privatizing it or dismissing the need for metaphysical guidance.
ASAD-NOTES:96:9#n5/r3.anchor: the purport of the above passage goes far beyond any historical incident or situation

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p173#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p173#3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p173#3/r1.claim: The one who forbids prayer is Abū Jahl; Abū Hurayra reports his threat to step on Muḥammad's neck if he saw him praying, which occasioned these verses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p173#3/r1.anchor: يعني: أبا جهل (9)، قال أبو هريرة: قال أبو جهل: لأن رأيت محمدا # -صلى الله عليه وسلم- يصلي لأطأن على رقبته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p173#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p173#3/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p173#3/r2.claim: Here araʾayta expresses amazement to the listener, and repetition intensifies the astonishing nature of the scene.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p173#3/r2.anchor: ومعنى: أرأيت هاهنا تعجيب للمخاطب، وكرر هذه اللفظة للتأكيد في العجيب.

WAHIDI-QT:96:10/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:96:10/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:96:10/r1.claim: Abu Jahl threatened that if he saw Muhammad praying, he would trample his neck.
WAHIDI-QT:96:10/r1.anchor: { عبدا إذا صلى } وذلك أنه قال : لئن رأيت محمدا يصلي لأطأن على رقبته

WAHIDI-QT:96:10/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:96:10/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:96:10/r2.claim: Here “have you seen?” expresses amazement; the same rhetorical use applies to 96:11–12.
WAHIDI-QT:96:10/r2.anchor: ومعنى أرأيت ها هنا تعجب ،   وكذلك قوله { أرأيت إن كان على الهدى } { أو أمر بالتقوى }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r2.claim: Abu Jahl threatened to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him praying.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r2.anchor: وذلك أنه قال: لئن رأيت محمدا يصلي لأطأن على رقبته،

ELMALILI:96:9-19/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r3.speaker: İbn Atıyye
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya says exegetes agree that the praying servant is the Messenger and the person forbidding him is Abu Jahl.
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r3.anchor: İbn Atıyye’nin beyânına göre burada namaz kılan bir abdden murad Resûlullah, nehyeden de Ebû Cehil olduğunda müfessirîn ihtilâf etmemişlerdir

ELMALILI:96:9-19/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r4.claim: The shift from recitation to prayer is apt because recitation is a prayer pillar and prayer is the foundation of worship and pillar of religion; this shows the verses came after prayer was legislated.
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r4.anchor: Kıraatten bahsolunurken namaza geçilmesi onda kıraatin bir rükün olması

ELMALILI:96:9-19/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r5.speaker: Ebû Hüreyre
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Abu Jahl swore by Lat and Uzza to trample and soil the Prophet’s face if he saw him pray; approaching, he recoiled, describing a fiery trench, terror, and wings, and the Prophet said angels would tear him apart.
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r5.anchor: Ebû Hüreyre’den rivayetlerinde: Ebû Cehil Resûlullah’ı namaz kılarken görürse muhakkak boynunu çiğneyip yüzünü sürteceğine dair

ELMALILI:96:9-19/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r6.speaker: Tirmizî
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r6.claim: Tirmidhi’s version has Abu Jahl approach the praying Prophet, repeating that he had forbidden him to do this.
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r6.anchor: Tirmizî’nin rivayetinde de [5957] Peygamber namaz kılarken Ebû Cehil

ELMALILI:96:9-19/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r7.speaker: Hasan
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r7.claim: The author rejects Hasan’s report that Umayya forbade Salman to pray: Salman embraced Islam in Medina after the Hijra, whereas the sura is agreed to be Meccan.
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r7.anchor: Hasan’dan mervî olan rivayet sahih olamaz. Çünkü Selman’ın islâmı hicretten sonra Medine’de olduğunda hilâf bulunmadığı gibi, sûrenin Mekkî olduğunda da hilâf yoktur

ELMALILI:96:9-19/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r8.claim: Although the occasion concerned Abu Jahl, the verse’s general ruling also covers anyone like Bilal who is stopped from prayer.
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r8.anchor: âyetin hükmü âm olduğu için ona ve emsâline de şâmil olacağında şüphe yoktur

ELMALILI:96:9-19/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r9.speaker: Tebrizî
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r9.claim: Tabrizi reports that salat here meant the noon prayer, the first congregational prayer in Islam, performed by Abu Bakr, Ali, and early Muslims when Abu Talib arrived with Ja‘far and urged him to join them.
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r9.anchor: Tebrizî demiş ki: “Burada ‘salât’tan murad öğle namazıdır

ELMALILI:96:9-19/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r10.speaker: Ebû Tâlib
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r10.claim: In verses cited by Tabrizi, Abu Talib declares he will not abandon the Prophet and urges Ali and Ja‘far to support their cousin.
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r10.anchor: Ebû Tâlib şu beyitleri söylüyordu: إِنَّ عَلِيًّا وَجَعْفَرًا ثِقَتِ ي عِنْدَ مُلِمِّ الزَّمَانِ وَالْكُرَ بِ وَاللّٰهَِّ لاَ أَخْذُلُ النَّبِيَّ

ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r1.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r1.claim: Alusi objects that prayer became obligatory only on the Night Journey, which he places after Abu Talib’s death; he cites chronologies placing Isra one to five years before the Hijra and Abu Talib’s death three years before it.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r1.anchor: Âlûsî der ki: “Bunda nazar vardır. Çünkü namaz hiç hilâfsız İsrâ gecesinde farz kılınmıştır. İsrâ’ın hicretten bir sene evvel olduğuna da İbn Hazm icmâ‘iddia etmiştir

ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r2.claim: The author finds Alusi’s objection unpersuasive: Isra established the five daily prayers, while earlier legislation of other prayers, such as night vigil or a noon prayer, remains possible.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r2.anchor: Çünkü İsrâ’da farz kılınan mutlak namaz değil, beş vakit namazdır. Binâen‘aleyh ondan evvel Müzzemmil’de geçtiği vechile gece kıyâmının farz olması gibi bir öğle namazının da farz kılınmış olmasına münâfî olmaz

ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r3.claim: The cited account calls it the noon prayer without explicitly saying it was obligatory; the prayer said to have first been performed publicly after Umar’s conversion was likely this one.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r3.anchor: mezkur rivayette salât-i zuhr denilmiş, farz olduğu tasrih de olunmamıştır. Hazret-i Ömer’in islâmı üzerine ilk olarak alenen kılındığı rivayet olunan namaz da bu olmak gerektir

ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r4.claim: Even if the occasion involved noon prayer, the unrestricted verse covers forbidding any legally prescribed or voluntary prayer, since the prohibition targets prayer itself.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r4.anchor: âyette de murad yalnız odur demek doğru olmaz. Çünkü âyet mutlaktır. Meşrû‘olan herhangi bir namaza şâmildir. Gerek farz ve gerek nâfile herhangi bir namazdan nehiy

ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r5.claim: A prohibition due to an accompanying circumstance such as a disliked time or usurped place differs, because it concerns time or place rather than prayer itself.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r5.anchor: Meğer ki esâs-ı nehy namazın kendisinden değil de ahvâl-i mukārinesinden biri itibariyle olsun o vakit câiz olabilir

ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r6.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r6.claim: Ali saw people praying before the Eid prayer and said he had not seen the Messenger do that; when asked why he did not forbid them, he feared falling under this threat.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r6.anchor: Hazret-i Ali kerremallahu vecheh musallâda bayram namazından evvel namaz kılan bazı kimseleri gördüğü zaman “Resûlullah’ı böyle yaparken görmedim” demiş

ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r7.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r7.claim: In another report, Ali says he does not wish to forbid a person from praying, but will tell them what he saw the Messenger do.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r7.anchor: Diğer bir rivayette de “bir kulu namaz kılarken nehyetmeyi arzu [5959] etmem

ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r8.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r8.claim: Abu Hanifa answers Abu Yusuf’s question about a supplication after bowing by prescribing “Our Lord, praise belongs to You,” without explicitly forbidding the alternative, illustrating caution about prohibition.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r8.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe rahmetullahi aleyh Hazretleri, kendisine İmam Ebû Yûsuf “musallî rükûdan başını kaldırırken اَللّٰهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي der mi?” diye sorduğu zaman

ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r9.claim: Forbidding other acts of worship is analogous to forbidding prayer; verbal prohibition and stopping someone through conduct are alike, so distracting someone from worship also falls under the threat, as with Abu Jahl.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r9.anchor: Sâir ibadetlerden nehiy de namazdan nehye kıyas olunur. Bu babda kavlen nehy ile fiilen ve hâlen nehiy arasında fark da yoktur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r1.speaker: Müfessirlerin çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r1.claim: Most exegetes take these verses as a rebuke to Abu Jahl for trying to stop Muhammad and believers from praying at the Kaaba.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r1.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’e hitap ederek onun ve müminlerin Kâbe önünde namaz kılmalarını engellemeye kalkışan Ebû Cehil’e karşı bir eleştiri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r2.claim: A universal reading is more suitable: all tyrants in every age who obstruct religion's work of shaping social life by goodness, truth, and justice are criticized.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r2.anchor: her dönemde görülen ve dinin sosyal hayatı iyilik, hak ve adalet ilkeleri yönünde şekillendirme işlevini engellemek isteyen bütün zorbaların eleştirildiği

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:9-10:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:9-10:anmerkung/r2.speaker: Nöldeke and Schwally
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:9-10:anmerkung/r2.claim: Nöldeke and Schwally insist that ʿabd means God's servant, not merely a human being; inner-textual indications of unequal rank support the social reading of slave as well.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:9-10:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Nöldeke und Schwally vertreten mit aller Entschiedenheit die erste Alternative

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:9-10:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:9-10:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:9-10:anmerkung/r3.claim: ʿAbd can mean both slave and worshipper: the worldly view sees a slave, while the believer recognizes God's servant, who may owe obedience to God over an earthly master.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:9-10:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Die Doppelbedeutung des Wortes ʿabd bringt den damit eingeforderten Perspektivwechsel gleichsam auf den Punkt

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:9-10:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:9-10:anmerkung/r4.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:9-10:anmerkung/r4.claim: Neuwirth also conjectures that ʿabd may refer to the preacher himself.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:9-10:anmerkung/r4.anchor: Neuwirth mutmaßt, der Ausdruck ʿabd könne auch den Verkünder selbst meinen

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p388/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p388/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p388/r3.claim: Those who stop the Prophet or other Muslims from prayer exemplify the earlier rebellion; prayer is a person’s foremost duty to God and deserves respect.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p389/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p389/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p389/r1.claim: The expression ‘have you seen’ directs attention to something improper or criticizes the perpetrator, like ‘just look at him’ in English.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p389/r1.anchor: are its equivalents in the English language

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p389/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p389/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p389/r2.claim: The description need not refer to one named person: multiple Quraysh ruffians, not only Abu Jahl, stopped the Prophet and other servants of God from prayer.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384/r1.claim: Abū Jahl threatened to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him praying; people called Abū Jahl the Pharaoh of this community.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى ﴾ قال قال أبو جهل لئن رأيت محمدا يصلي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r1.speaker: المفسرون
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r1.claim: As Ibn ʿAṭiyya says, commentators agree that the worshipper is the Messenger and the one who forbids prayer is Abu Jahl.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r1.anchor: ولم يختلف المفسرون كما قال ابن عطية في أن العبد المصلي هو رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم والناهي هو اللعين أبو جهل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Abu Jahl swore by al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā to trample the Prophet's neck and soil his face if he saw him praying; when he approached, he recoiled from a fiery trench and wings, and the Prophet said angels would have seized him limb by limb; the passage was then revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن أبا جهل حلف باللات والعزى لئن رأى رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يصلي ليطأن على رقبته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r3.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the forbidding man as Umayya ibn Khalaf, who prohibited Salmān from praying; al-Alusi says this is scarcely sound because Salmān converted in Medina and the sura is Meccan.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r3.anchor: وقول الحسن هو أمية بن خلف كان ينهى سلمان عن الصلاة لا يكاد يصح لأنه لا خلاف في أن إسلام سلمان

ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the prayer was the noon prayer and reports that it was performed in congregation, the first congregation in Islam, with the Prophet, Abū Bakr, and ʿAlī.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r4.anchor: الصلاة التي أشارت إليها الآية كانت على ما حكى أبو حيان صلاة الظهر وحكى أيضا أنها كانت تصلي جماعة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān also recounts that Abū Ṭālib and Jaʿfar passed by, Abū Ṭālib told his son to pray beside his cousin, and he left delighted, reciting a poem pledging support.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r5.anchor: فمر أبو طالب ومعه ابنه جعفر فقال له يا بني صل جناح ابن عمك وانصرف مسرورا وأنشأ يقول

ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r6.claim: The chronology challenges the Abū Ṭālib story: prayer was prescribed on the Night Journey before the Hijra, whereas Abū Ṭālib died about three years before it; later dating the Night Journey after five years is disputed.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r6.anchor: لأن الصلاة فرضت ليلة الإسراء بلا خلاف وادعى ابن حزم الإجماع على أنه كان قبل الهجرة بسنة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r7.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says Abu Jahl verbally confronted the Prophet during prayer, saying, Did I not forbid you? This supports taking the prohibition as explicit speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال كان النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يصلي فجاء أبو جهل فقال ألم أنهك عن هذا ألم أنهك عن هذا الحديث

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r10.claim: The one who forbids a servant to pray is Abu Jahl, and the servant is the Prophet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r10.anchor: أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى} نزلت في أبي جهل، نهى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الصلاة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r11.claim: Abu Jahl threatened to trample the Prophet while praying, but recoiled from a trench of fire, terror, and wings; the Prophet said angels would seize him limb by limb. The report is uncertain about whether the revelation was in Abu Hurayra's narration or another source.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r11.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال أبو جهل: هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r1.claim: The verses were revealed about Abū Jahl, who threatened to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him prostrating, then retreated and described a trench of fire, terror, and wings between them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r1.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل قال لو رأيت محمدا ساجدا لوطئت عنقه

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r2.claim: The generic indefinite “a servant” intensifies the ugliness of forbidding prayer and magnifies the worshipper's servitude.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r2.anchor: ولفظ العبد وتنكيره للمبالغة في تقبيح النهي والدلالة على كمال عبودية المنهي

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.claim: A report promises the reciter a reward as though he had recited the entire set of shorter suras.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصل كله

BINTSHATI:v2p26/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p26/r3.speaker: جمهرة المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v2p26/r3.claim: Most exegetes identify the man forbidding prayer as Abu Jahl, who prevented Muhammad from worshiping God.
BINTSHATI:v2p26/r3.anchor: وجمهرة المفسرين على ان هذه الآيات، إلى آخر السورة، نزلت في "أبي جهل ابن هشام"

BINTSHATI:v2p26/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p26/r4.speaker: الحسن البصري
BINTSHATI:v2p26/r4.claim: A report from al-Hasan al-Basri instead identifies Umayya ibn Khalaf as the man forbidding Salman al-Farisi from praying.
BINTSHATI:v2p26/r4.anchor: وفي قول عن الحسن البصري: هو أمية بن خلف، كان ينهي سلمان - الفارسي - عن الصلاة

BINTSHATI:v2p26/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p26/r5.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI:v2p26/r5.claim: Al-Tabari recounts Abu Jahl’s threat to trample Muhammad at prayer and Abu Jahl’s retreat, saying a trench of fire stood between them; no grading or chain is stated.
BINTSHATI:v2p26/r5.anchor: قيل فأتى أبو جهل رسول الله وهو يصلي ليطأ على رقبته فما لبث أن رجع عنه ونكص على عقبيه

BINTSHATI:v2p26/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p26/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p26/r6.claim: The Abu Jahl occasion raises a chronological problem for the view that all of al-Alaq was first revealed, before Muhammad had begun preaching or been threatened.
BINTSHATI:v2p26/r6.anchor: دون أن يعرضوا لما يرد على هذا، من المشهور في أن سورة العلق هي أول ما نزل من الوحي

BINTSHATI:v2p27/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r1.claim: Continuing al-Razi’s first solution, the rest of the surah came later about Abu Jahl, and the Prophet was directed to place these verses at its beginning.
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r1.anchor: نزلت البقية في أبي جهل بن هشام، وأمر الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بضمها إلى أول السورة

BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.claim: Al-Razi’s second solution reads الإنسان generically: despite creation and blessings, people transgress, forget their return, and forbid worship when they should follow guidance and enjoin piety.
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.anchor: أن تحمل الآيات على عموم لفظها في الظاهر، وهو أن الإنسان، جملة الإنسان، خلقه الله من علق

BINTSHATI:v2p27/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r3.claim: Both explanations are possible; the sequence suggests the passage followed public preaching and prayer, while a specific occasion does not prevent the wording from applying generally.
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r3.anchor: وكلا الوجهين جائز. فسياق الآيات في السورة، يشعر بأنها نزلت بعد أن أبلغ المصطفى رسالة ربه

BINTSHATI:v2p27/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari makes the conditional clause in verse 13 the second object of arayta in verse 9, treats arayta before the condition as extra, and takes verse 14 as the condition’s answer.
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r4.anchor: ذهب الزمخشري في (الكشاف) إلى أن الجملة الشرطية في {أَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى}

BINTSHATI:v2p27/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r5.claim: She objects that this analysis inserts an extra arayta into the flow and leaves an interrogative response unprefixed by fa, contrary to the grammarians’ rule.
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r5.anchor: تبدو فيه {أَرَأَيْتَ} في الجملة الشرطية مقحمة على السياق، تمت للزمخشري تسوية الصنعة

BINTSHATI:v2p28/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r1.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects al-Zamakhshari’s analysis, holding that arayta’s second object must be an interrogative sentence, a construction frequent in the Quran.
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r1.anchor: وكذلك رفض مذهب الزمخشري في جعل {أَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَرَى} جواباً لشرط {إِنْ كَذَّبَ}

BINTSHATI:v2p28/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r3.claim: She argues that Quranic interrogative arayta usually omits its second object and directs attention instead to the lesson or warning; she cites several Meccan examples.
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r3.anchor: وإنما يستغنى عن هذا المفعول، بتقرير يلفت إلى موضع العبرة والنذير

BINTSHATI:v2p29/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r2.claim: The repeated arayta in this passage is a stylistic prompt to see and reflect on the warning; it need not take an explicit or inferred second object.
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r2.anchor: فلفتت إلى ما هو جدير بالرؤية والبصر والتدبر، وأغنت عما تعلق به النجاة من مفعول ثان

BINTSHATI:v2p30/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r3.claim: She urges readers to notice Quranic stylistic patterns even when they depart from school grammar and rhetoric, rather than forcing them into technical rules by conjecture.
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r3.anchor: فيشغلنا عن البيان العالى، تسوية الصنعة النحوية أو البلاغية، بالتأويل فيه والتقدير

BIQAI-FULL:v8p483/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p483/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p483/r7.claim: Calling the worshipper a servant intensifies the condemnation: he is God's slave, and prayer is service to the Lord whose sovereignty no one can deny.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p483/r7.anchor: قال معبرا بالعبودية منكرا للمبالغة في تقبيح النهي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p483/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p483/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p483/r8.claim: Prayer is the greatest form of worship because it joins the servant to God while entirely detaching him from creation; forbidding it denies God His due, perhaps from envy or transgression.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p483/r8.anchor: وهي أعظم أنواع العبادة لأنها مع كونها أقرب وصلة إلى الحق

TAB:96:10/r2.speaker: author
TAB:96:10/r2.claim: The person being forbidden is Muhammad, whom Abu Jahl barred from praying at the Station; the passage exposes Abu Jahl's audacity in opposing prayer while rejecting God's favor.
TAB:96:10/r2.anchor: أبا جهل الذي ينهاك أن تصلي عند المقام

TAB:96:10/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:10/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:96:10/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies Abu Jahl as the one who forbade Muhammad when he prayed.
TAB:96:10/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح ،   عن مجاهد ،   في قول الله :  { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى } قال :  أبو جهل

TAB:96:10/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:10/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB:96:10/r4.claim: Qatada says the passage was revealed about God's enemy Abu Jahl, who threatened to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him praying.
TAB:96:10/r4.anchor: عن قتادة { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى } نزلت في عدو الله أبي جهل

TAB:96:10/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:10/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB:96:10/r5.claim: Qatada transmits a saying that every nation has a Pharaoh and Abu Jahl was the Pharaoh of this community.
TAB:96:10/r5.anchor: عن معمر ،   عن قتادة ،   في قول الله :  { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى }

TAB:96:10/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:10/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:96:10/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says Muhammad was praying when Abu Jahl came and forbade him, and the verses through 96:16 were then revealed.
TAB:96:10/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قال :  كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي ،   فجاءه أبو جهل

ITQAN:v4p394/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p394/r14.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p394/r14.claim: The one forbidding a servant is Abu Jahl, and the servant is the Prophet.
ITQAN:v4p394/r14.anchor: 5770 ﴿ الذي ينهى عبدا ﴾ هو أبو جهل والعبد هو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p91/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p91/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p91/r2.claim: Verse endings are not always self-contained semantic units: meaning comes first, and a fāṣila may depend on what precedes or follows it.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p91/r2.anchor: ليست الفواصل هي دائماً تامة المعنى فقد تكون متعلقة بما قبلها أوما بعدها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p541/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p541/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p541/r3.claim: A Qur'anic verse ending is not always a complete semantic unit: it may remain attached to what precedes or follows, as in these examples.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p541/r3.anchor: الآيات ليست وحدات مستقلة المعنى قد تكون تامة وقد تكون متعلقة بما قبلها أو بعدها

IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r1.speaker: أبو جهل
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the warning passage 96:9-19 was revealed about Abu Jahl, what he said, and his attempt to stop the Prophet while he prayed.
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r1.anchor: وأنزل عليه فيما قال أبو جهل بن هشام، وما هم به: أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى

ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says exegetes unanimously identify the forbidding person as Abu Jahl and the worshipping servant as Muhammad.
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطية : ولم يختلف أحد من المفسرين أن الناهي أبو جهل ، وأن العبد المصلي وهو محمد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، انتهى

ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r2.claim: Al-Hasan, as quoted in the Kashshaf, identifies the forbidding person as Umayya ibn Khalaf, who forbade Salman to pray.
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r2.anchor: وفي الكشاف ، وقال الحسن : هو أمية بن خلف ، كان ينهى سلمان عن الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r3.speaker: التبريزي
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r3.claim: Al-Tabrizi says the prayer meant here is the noon prayer.
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r3.anchor: وقال التبريزي : المراد بالصلاة هنا صلاة الظهر

ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r4.claim: An account calls this the first congregational prayer in Islam: Muhammad prayed with Abu Bakr, Ali, and other early believers when Abu Talib and Jaʿfar passed by.
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r4.anchor: قيل : هي أول جماعة أقيمت في الإسلام ، كان معه أبو بكر وعليّ وجماعة من السابقين ، فمرّ به أبو طالب ومعه ابنه جعفر

ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r5.speaker: أبو طالب
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r5.claim: Abu Talib urged Ali and Jaʿfar to support and defend their cousin the Prophet, then departed happily; he composed verses pledging not to abandon the Prophet and urging his sons to defend him.
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r5.anchor: فقال له : صل جناح ابن عمك وانصرف مسروراً ، وأنشأ أبو طالب يقول : إن علياً وجعفراً ثقتي

ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r6.claim: The apparent addressee of the first and second أرأيت is the Messenger; the pronouns remain consistent on this reading.
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r6.anchor: والخطاب في { أرأيت } الظاهر أنه للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم ، وكذا { أرأيت } الثاني ، والتناسق في الضمائر هو الذي يقتضيه النظم

ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r7.claim: Another reading shifts the address to the disbeliever: if the worshipper's prayer is guidance and a call to God and piety, would he still forbid him? In this reading the conditional pronouns refer to the forbidding person.
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r7.anchor: وقيل : { أرأيت } خطاب للكافر التفت إلى الكافر فقال : أرأيت يا كافر ، إن كانت صلاته هدى ودعاء إلى الله

ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r8.speaker: ابن عطية والفراء
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya and al-Farraʾ take the pronoun in if he is on guidance to refer to the worshipper, not the forbidding person.
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : الضمير في { إن كان على الهدى } عائد على المصلي ، وقاله الفراء وغيره

ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari frames an ironic conditional: if the forbidding man were on a sound path and enjoining what he regards as piety, or instead denying truth and turning from true religion, does he not know God sees and requites him? This is a threat.
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r9.anchor: قال الزمخشري : ومعناه أخبرني عن من ينهى بعض عباد الله عن صلاته إن كان ذلك الناهي على طريقة سديدة

ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r10.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r10.claim: Al-Farraʾ calls the situation astonishing and a rebuke: Abu Jahl forbids a worshipper who follows guidance and piety, while the forbidding man denies and turns away; God sees his deed.
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r10.anchor: قال الفراء : المعنى { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } ، وهو على الهدى وأمر بالتقوى ، والناهي مكذب متول عن الذكر ، أي فما أعجب هذا

ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r11.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r11.claim: Al-Farraʾ explains that piety is paired with prayer because Abu Jahl objected both to the Prophet's prayer and call to God; the Prophet reformed himself through prayer and others through enjoining piety.
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r11.anchor: لأن أبا جهل كان يشق عليه من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أمر أن : الصلاة والدعاء إلى الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r12.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says the closing question ألم يعلم completes the reproach and threat for each of the three preceding conditional formulations, compressing what could otherwise be stated after each.
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : { ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى } : إكمال التوبيخ والوعيد بحسب التوفيقات الثلاثة يصلح مع كل واحد منها

ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhshari assigns the relative clause and conditional sentence as أرأيت's two objects, omits the first conditional answer in favor of the second, and treats the middle repeated أرأيت as emphatic.
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r13.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : فإن قلت : ما متعلق { أرأيت } ؟ قلت : { الذي ينهى } مع الجملة الشرطية ، وهما في موضع المفعولين

ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r14.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects that parsing: the second object of أرأيت must be an interrogative clause, as in Qur'anic examples, rather than the relative plus conditional proposed by al-Zamakhshari.
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r14.anchor: وعندنا أن المفعول الثاني لا يكون إلا جملة استفهامية ، كقوله : { أفرأيت الذي تولى وأعطى قليلاً وأكدى أعنده علم الغيب }

ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r15.claim: Abū Ḥayyān instead parses the first أرأيت with the relative as its first object; the later two instances have omitted objects recoverable from the servant or forbidding man and from the final interrogative clause.
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r15.anchor: ويجعل مفعول { أرأيت } الأولى هو الموصول ، وجاء بعده { أرأيت } ، وهي تطلب مفعولين ، وأرأيت الثانية كذلك

ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r16.claim: The successive omissions are not a case of syntactic competition, since clauses cannot be pronominally omitted; they are ordinary ellipses.
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r16.anchor: وهؤلاء الطوالب ليس طلبها على طريق التنازع ، لأن الجمل لا يصح إضمارها ، وإنما ذلك من باب الحذف في غير التنازع

ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r17.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhshari's allowance of an interrogative clause as a conditional answer without fa: grammarians require fa after a construction involving a request, except in poetic necessity.
ABUHAYYAN:96:9/r17.anchor: وأما تجويز الزمخشري وقوع جملة الاستفهام جواباً للشرط بغير فاء ، فلا أعلم أحداً أجازه ، بل نصوا على وجوب الفاء

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan instead identifies the forbider as Umayya ibn Khalaf, who prevented Salmān from praying.
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r2.anchor: وفي الكشاف ، وقال الحسن : هو أمية بن خلف ، كان ينهى سلمان عن الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r3.speaker: التبريزي

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r3.anchor: وقال التبريزي : المراد بالصلاة هنا صلاة الظهر

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r4.claim: An anonymous report calls this Islam’s first congregational prayer, attended by Abū Bakr, ʿAlī, and other early Muslims; Abū Ṭālib and Jaʿfar arrived, Abū Ṭālib urged support for the Prophet, and the Prophet rejoiced at his verses.
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r4.anchor: قيل : هي أول جماعة أقيمت في الإسلام ، كان معه أبو بكر وعليّ وجماعة من السابقين

ABUHAYYAN:96:12/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطية : ولم يختلف أحد من المفسرين أن الناهي أبو جهل ، وأن العبد المصلي وهو محمد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
