ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r4.anchor: قيل : هي أول جماعة أقيمت في الإسلام ، كان معه أبو بكر وعليّ وجماعة من السابقين

ALUSI:96:10/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī presents the prohibition of a servant at prayer as one consequence of human tyranny, accompanied by a warning.
ALUSI:96:10/r1.anchor: ذكر لبعض آثار الطغيان ووعيد عليها

ALUSI:96:10/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI:96:10/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the commentators agree that the praying servant is the Messenger and the prohibiter is Abū Jahl.
ALUSI:96:10/r2.anchor: كما قال ابن عطية في أن العبد المصلي هو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والناهي هو اللعين أبو جهل

ALUSI:96:10/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI:96:10/r3.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that Abū Jahl swore by al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā to trample and soil the praying Prophet, then recoiled, described a fiery trench, terror and wings, and heard the Prophet warn that angels would seize him; 96:6 through the sūra was revealed.
ALUSI:96:10/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن أبا جهل حلف باللات والعزى لئن رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي

ALUSI:96:10/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r4.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI:96:10/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the forbidden worshipper as Salmān and the prohibiter as Umayya ibn Khalaf.
ALUSI:96:10/r4.anchor: وقول الحسن هو أمية بن خلف كان ينهى سلمان عن الصلاة لا يكاد يصح

ALUSI:96:10/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī doubts al-Ḥasan’s identification because Salmān converted in Medina after the Hijra, whereas the sūra is Meccan.
ALUSI:96:10/r5.anchor: لا خلاف في أن إسلام سلمان رضي الله تعالى عنه كان بالمدينة بعد الهجرة كما أنه لا خلاف في أن السورة مكية

ALUSI:96:10/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r6.claim: The warning applies generally: if Umayya’s reported incident occurred, he too falls under the verse’s ruling.
ALUSI:96:10/r6.anchor: نعم حكم الآية عام فإن كان ما حكي عن أمية واقعاً فحكمها شامل له

ALUSI:96:10/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r7.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:10/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the prayer alluded to was the noon prayer.
ALUSI:96:10/r7.anchor: على ما حكى أبو حيان صلاة الظهر

ALUSI:96:10/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:10/r8.claim: An account says the prayer was congregational and the first congregation established in Islam, with the Prophet, Abū Bakr and ʿAlī present.
ALUSI:96:10/r8.anchor: وحكي أيضاً أنها كانت تصلي جماعة وهي أول جماعة أقيمت في الإسلام

ALUSI:96:10/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r9.speaker: أبو طالب
ALUSI:96:10/r9.claim: In the same account, Abū Ṭālib passes with Jaʿfar, tells him to join his cousin in prayer, and leaves pleased.
ALUSI:96:10/r9.anchor: فمر أبو طالب ومعه ابنه جعفر فقال له يا بني صل جناح ابن عمك وانصرف مسروراً

ALUSI:96:10/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r10.speaker: أبو طالب
ALUSI:96:10/r10.claim: Abū Ṭālib’s poem calls ʿAlī and Jaʿfar dependable in hardship and urges them not to abandon the Prophet, their cousin and maternal and paternal brother.
ALUSI:96:10/r10.anchor: فمر أبو طالب ومعه ابنه جعفر فقال له يا بني صل جناح ابن عمك وانصرف مسروراً وأنشأ

ALUSI:96:10/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r11.claim: Al-Ālūsī notes that prayer was made obligatory on the Night Journey, a chronology that complicates the report involving Abū Ṭālib.
ALUSI:96:10/r11.anchor: لأن الصلاة فرضت ليلة الإسراء بلا خلاف

ALUSI:96:10/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r12.speaker: ابن حزم
ALUSI:96:10/r12.claim: Ibn Ḥazm claims consensus that the Night Journey occurred one year before the Hijra.
ALUSI:96:10/r12.anchor: وادعى ابن حزم الإجماع على أنه كان قبل الهجرة بسنة

ALUSI:96:10/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r13.speaker: ابن فارس
ALUSI:96:10/r13.claim: Ibn Fāris fixes the Night Journey at one year and three months before the Hijra.
ALUSI:96:10/r13.anchor: وجزم ابن فارس بأنه كان قبلها بسنة وثلاثة أشهر

ALUSI:96:10/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r14.speaker: السدي
ALUSI:96:10/r14.claim: Al-Suddī dates the Night Journey to one year and five months before the Hijra.

ALUSI:96:10/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r15.claim: Al-Ālūsī says Abū Ṭālib died about three years before the Hijra, three or five days before Khadīja, whose death was ten years after the mission on the sound view; thus Abū Ṭālib would not have witnessed prayer’s obligation.
ALUSI:96:10/r15.anchor: وموت أبي طالب كان قبل الهجرة بنحو ثلاث سنين لأنه كان قبل وفاة خديجة بثلاثة وقيل بخمسة أيام

ALUSI:96:10/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r16.speaker: الزهري
ALUSI:96:10/r16.claim: Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ transmits al-Zuhrī’s view that the Night Journey was five years after the beginning of the prophetic mission; al-Nawawī and al-Qurṭubī prefer it, though objections were raised.
ALUSI:96:10/r16.anchor: حكى القاضي عياض عن الزهري ورجحه النووي والقرطبي أن الإسراء كان بعد البعث بخمس سنين

ALUSI:96:10/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r17.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:10/r17.claim: One explanation takes the prohibiting as preventing; the wording hints that Abū Jahl lacked power to do more.
ALUSI:96:10/r17.anchor: والنهي قيل بمعنى المنع وعبر به إشارة إلى عدم اقتدار اللعين على غير ذلك

ALUSI:96:10/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:96:10/r18.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Abū Jahl came upon the Prophet at prayer and twice challenged him, “Did I not forbid you?” Al-Tirmidhī and others authenticate the report.
ALUSI:96:10/r18.anchor: وصححه وغيرهما عن ابن عباس قال «كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي فجاء أبو جهل

ALUSI:96:10/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r19.claim: The present-tense form evokes the past scene as if it were occurring now, underscoring its strangeness.
ALUSI:96:10/r19.anchor: والتعبير بما يفيد الاستقبال لاستحضار الصورة الماضية لنوع غرابة

ALUSI:96:10/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r20.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:10/r20.claim: One view takes the seeing in the opening question as inward, and likewise in the question at 96:13.
ALUSI:96:10/r20.anchor: والرؤية قيل قلبية وكذا في قوله تعالى : { أَرَءيْتَ إِن كَذَّبَ وتولى }

ALUSI:96:10/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r21.claim: The three questions assign the relative clause as the first object of the first; the first objects of the second and third are omitted pronouns or demonstratives, while the third’s second object is “Does he not know that God sees?”, elided after the first two.
ALUSI:96:10/r21.anchor: والمفعول الأول للأول الموصول وللثاني والثالث محذوف وهو ضمير يعود عليه أو اسم إشارة يشار به إليه

ALUSI:96:10/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r22.claim: This is not grammatical tanāzuʿ: whole clauses cannot be elided; the construction is semantic government with deletion outside tanāzuʿ.
ALUSI:96:10/r22.anchor: وليس ذلك من التنازع لأن الجمل لا يصح إضمارها وإنما هو من الطلب المعنوي والحذف في غير التنازع

ALUSI:96:10/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r26.speaker: جمع
ALUSI:96:10/r26.claim: A group takes the address throughout as directed to anyone capable of understanding.
ALUSI:96:10/r26.anchor: والخطاب في الكل على ما اختاره جمع لكل من يصلح أن يكون مخاطباً ممن له مسكة

ALUSI:96:10/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r27.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:10/r27.claim: Another view addresses humanity generally, like the address at 96:8.
ALUSI:96:10/r27.anchor: والخطاب في الكل على ما اختاره جمع لكل من يصلح أن يكون مخاطباً ممن له مسكة وقيل للإنسان

ALUSI:96:10/r28.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r28.speaker: بعض
ALUSI:96:10/r28.claim: Some take the indefinite nunation of “a servant” at face value.
ALUSI:96:10/r28.anchor: وتنوين { عبداً } على ما هو ظاهر كلام البعض للتنكير

ALUSI:96:10/r29.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r29.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:10/r29.claim: Another reading takes the nunation as magnifying the Prophet, the prohibition’s enormity, and the astonishment it deserves.
ALUSI:96:10/r29.anchor: ولذا قيل عبداً ولم يقل نبياً مجتبى

ALUSI:96:10/r30.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r30.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r30.claim: Restricting the prohibition by the temporal phrase suggests that it concerns prayer while the worshipper is engaged in it.
ALUSI:96:10/r30.anchor: وتقييد النهي بالظرف يشعر بأن النهي عن الصلاة حال التلبس بها

ALUSI:96:10/r31.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r31.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r31.claim: The clauses are separated to intensify rebuke and warning and show that each has an independent point.
ALUSI:96:10/r31.anchor: وفصل بين الجمل للاعتناء بأمر التشنيع والوعيد حيث أشعر أن كل جملة مقصودة على حيالها

ALUSI:96:10/r32.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r32.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r32.claim: First the passage warns generally against forbidding prayer: does the prohibiter not know God sees and will punish him?
ALUSI:96:10/r32.anchor: فشنع سبحانه على الناهي أولاً بنهيه عن الصلاة وأوعد عليه مطلقاً

ALUSI:96:10/r38.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r38.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:10/r38.claim: An alternative makes the first seeing visual and needing no second object, but the second and third inward; their conditional clauses fill the second-object position.
ALUSI:96:10/r38.anchor: وقيل إن الرؤية في الجملة الأولى بصرية فلا تحتاج إلى مفعول ثان

ALUSI:96:10/r40.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r40.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:10/r40.claim: Another analysis takes all three questions as inward seeing: the first conditional’s answer is omitted in favor of the second’s, while the third question independently opposes the first condition.
ALUSI:96:10/r40.anchor: وقيل إن أرأيت في الجمل الثلاث من الرؤية القلبية والمفعول الأول للأولى الموصول

ALUSI:96:10/r46.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r46.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r46.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the claim that the second object of “Have you seen?” must only be an interrogative clause, noting that this conflicts with what is reported as Sibawayh’s chosen view.
ALUSI:96:10/r46.anchor: مخالف لما صرحوا بأنه مختار سيبويه فلا يلتفت إليه

ALUSI:96:10/r47.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r47.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r47.claim: Some exclude both prohibiter and worshipper from the address on contextual grounds; al-Baḥr prefers the Prophet as addressee, while others allow the disbeliever, with the scene cast generally.
ALUSI:96:10/r47.anchor: ولم يجعلوا فيما ذكر الخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا للكافر الناهي لأن السياق مقتض لخروج الناهي والمنهي

ALUSI:96:10/r53.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r53.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI:96:10/r53.claim: The Imām allows the whole address to be to the Prophet: if the sensible, wealthy man had chosen guidance and piety, would that not have been better than disbelief and obstructing worship?
ALUSI:96:10/r53.anchor: وجوز الإمام كون الخطاب في الكل له عليه الصلاة والسلام وقال في بيان معنى

ALUSI:96:10/r54.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r54.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:96:10/r54.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn reads 96:9–10 as exposing tyranny when a person feels self-sufficient, 96:11–12 as rebuking lost guidance and piety, and 96:13–14 as rebuking earned punishment and distance from God.
ALUSI:96:10/r54.anchor: واعتبر عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع وما بعدها توبيخاً على كسب ما يضر

ALUSI:96:10/r55.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r55.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r55.claim: Al-Ālūsī distances himself from ʿIṣām al-Dīn’s elaboration, inviting reflection and leaving the matter to God’s intended meaning.
ALUSI:96:10/r55.anchor: وهو كما ترى فتأمل جميع ما تقدم والله تعالى بمراده أعلم

ALUSI:96:10/r56.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r56.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r56.claim: Everyone who forbids prayer shares the warning, not only Abū Jahl.
ALUSI:96:10/r56.anchor: ثم إن الآية وإن نزلت في أبي جهل عليه اللعنة لكن كل من نهى عن الصلاة ومنع منها فهو شريكه في الوعيد

ALUSI:96:10/r57.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r57.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r57.claim: This general warning does not bar forbidding prayer in a usurped place or at disliked times, because the actual objection concerns a concomitant attribute rather than prayer itself.
ALUSI:96:10/r57.anchor: ولا يلزم على ذلك المنع عن النهي عن الصلاة في الدار المغصوبة والأوقات المكروهة لأن المنهي عنه في الحقيقة ليس عن الصلاة نفسها

ALUSI:96:10/r58.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r58.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
ALUSI:96:10/r58.claim: ʿAlī, seeing people pray before the Eid prayer, says he had not seen the Messenger do that; when asked why he does not forbid them, he fears this warning, preferring to tell them what he witnessed.
ALUSI:96:10/r58.anchor: فروي عن أمير المؤمنين كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه رأى في المصلي أقواماً يصلون قبل صلاة العيد

ALUSI:96:10/r59.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r59.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI:96:10/r59.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa follows similar restraint: when Abū Yūsuf asks whether a worshipper should say “God forgive me” after bowing, he answers with the prescribed praise and prostration without explicitly forbidding it.
ALUSI:96:10/r59.anchor: وقد سلك نحو هذا المسلك أبو حنيفة عليه الرحمة فقد روي أن أبا يوسف قال له

ALUSI:96:10/r60.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r60.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r60.claim: The warning extends by analogy to forbidding other worship, whether by words or conduct, including distracting someone from worship—a common failing.
ALUSI:96:10/r60.anchor: ويقاس على النهي عن الصلاة النهي عن غيرها من أنواع العبادة ولا فرق بين النهي القالي والنهي الحالي

ALUSI:96:11/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI:96:11/r1.claim: Aḥmad, Muslim, al-Nasāʾī and others report from Abū Hurayra that Abū Jahl threatened the praying Prophet, recoiled at a trench of fire, terror and wings, and heard that angels would seize him; the sūra was then revealed from 96:6 to its end.
ALUSI:96:11/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن أبا جهل حلف باللات والعزى لئن رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي

ALUSI:96:11/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI:96:11/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the commentators agree that the servant being stopped from prayer is the Messenger and the forbidding man is Abū Jahl.
ALUSI:96:11/r2.anchor: كما قال ابن عطية في أن العبد المصلي هو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والناهي هو اللعين أبو جهل

ALUSI:96:11/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r3.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI:96:11/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the forbidding man as Umayya b. Khalaf, who stopped Salmān from praying; al-Ālūsī says this is hardly sound because Salmān embraced Islam in Medina while the sūra is Meccan.
ALUSI:96:11/r3.anchor: وقول الحسن هو أمية بن خلف كان ينهى سلمان عن الصلاة لا يكاد يصح لأنه لا خلاف

ALUSI:96:11/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:11/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān relates that the prayer in question was the noon prayer.

ALUSI:96:11/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:11/r5.claim: A further account calls it the first congregational prayer in Islam: the Prophet prayed with Abū Bakr and ʿAlī; Abū Ṭālib passed with Jaʿfar, urged him to join his cousin, and left pleased.
ALUSI:96:11/r5.anchor: وحكي أيضاً أنها كانت تصلي جماعة وهي أول جماعة أقيمت في الإسلام وأنه كان معه عليه الصلاة والسلام أبو بكر وعلي

ALUSI:96:11/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r6.speaker: أبو طالب
ALUSI:96:11/r6.claim: The cited poem attributed to Abū Ṭālib calls ʿAlī and Jaʿfar trusted kin in hardship and urges them not to abandon the Prophet but to support their maternal and paternal cousin.
ALUSI:96:11/r6.anchor: وأنشأ يقول : إن علياً وجعفراً ثقتي *** عند ملم الزمال والكرب

ALUSI:96:11/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:11/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī questions the Abū Ṭālib account: prayer was prescribed on the Night Journey, usually dated a year before the Hijra, whereas Abū Ṭālib died about three years before it. Reports place the Journey five years after the mission, a chronology criticized by others.
ALUSI:96:11/r7.anchor: وفي هذا نظر لأن الصلاة فرضت ليلة الإسراء بلا خلاف وادعى ابن حزم الإجماع على أنه كان قبل الهجرة بسنة

ALUSI:96:11/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r8.speaker: ابن حزم
ALUSI:96:11/r8.claim: Ibn Ḥazm claims consensus that the Night Journey was one year before the Hijra; Ibn Fāris gives one year and three months, and al-Suddī one year and five months.
ALUSI:96:11/r8.anchor: وادعى ابن حزم الإجماع على أنه كان قبل الهجرة بسنة وجزم ابن فارس بأنه كان قبلها بسنة وثلاثة أشهر وقال السدي

ALUSI:96:11/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r9.speaker: الزهري
ALUSI:96:11/r9.claim: Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ reports al-Zuhrī's view that the Night Journey occurred five years after the prophetic mission; al-Nawawī and al-Qurṭubī favor it, though al-Ālūsī notes objections to that dating.
ALUSI:96:11/r9.anchor: حكى القاضي عياض عن الزهري ورجحه النووي والقرطبي أن الإسراء كان بعد البعث بخمس سنين لكن قيل عليه ما قيل

ALUSI:96:11/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:11/r10.claim: Al-Ālūsī says nahy means forbidding; its wording suggests Abū Jahl could do no more than that, though some reports indicate he also verbally forbade the Prophet.
ALUSI:96:11/r10.anchor: والنهي قيل بمعنى المنع وعبر به إشارة إلى عدم اقتدار اللعين على غير ذلك

ALUSI:96:11/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:96:11/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Abū Jahl verbally told the Prophet, as he prayed, that he had forbidden him to do so; al-Tirmidhī authenticated this report.
ALUSI:96:11/r11.anchor: فقد أخرج أحمد والترمذي وصححه وغيرهما عن ابن عباس قال «كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي فجاء أبو جهل

ALUSI:96:11/r33.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r33.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:11/r33.claim: Although revealed about Abū Jahl, the warning applies to everyone who stops prayer. It does not forbid objecting to prayer in usurped places or disliked times, since the objection concerns an accompanying attribute rather than prayer itself.
ALUSI:96:11/r33.anchor: ثم إن الآية وإن نزلت في أبي جهل عليه اللعنة لكن كل من نهى عن الصلاة ومنع منها فهو شريكه في الوعيد

ALUSI:96:11/r34.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r34.speaker: علي
ALUSI:96:11/r34.claim: A report says ʿAlī saw people praying before the ʿĪd prayer; when asked why he did not forbid them, he feared the warning in this verse. Another version says he preferred to tell them what he had seen the Prophet do rather than forbid a worshipper.
ALUSI:96:11/r34.anchor: فروي عن أمير المؤمنين كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه رأى في المصلي أقواماً يصلون قبل صلاة العيد

ALUSI:96:11/r35.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r35.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI:96:11/r35.claim: Al-Ālūsī says Abū Ḥanīfa likewise avoided a direct prohibition: asked by Abū Yūsuf about a prayer formula while rising from bowing, he stated the formula he favored and continued to prostration without explicitly forbidding it.
ALUSI:96:11/r35.anchor: وقد سلك نحو هذا المسلك أبو حنيفة عليه الرحمة فقد روي أن أبا يوسف قال له أيقول المصلي حين يرفع رأسه

ALUSI:96:11/r36.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r36.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:11/r36.claim: The warning extends by analogy to forbidding other worship, whether by words or conduct; distracting someone from worship also counts as a practical prohibition, a widespread affliction.
ALUSI:96:11/r36.anchor: ويقاس على النهي عن الصلاة النهي عن غيرها من أنواع العبادة ولا فرق بين النهي القالي والنهي الحالي

BAGHAWI:96:9/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:9/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:9/r1.claim: The passage was revealed about Abu Jahl, who forbade the Prophet from praying.
BAGHAWI:96:9/r1.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل ، نهى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الصلاة

BAGHAWI:96:9/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:9/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI:96:9/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports Abu Jahl’s threat to trample Muhammad while praying, his recoil at an unseen trench of fire and wings, and the Prophet’s statement that angels would seize him; the narrator is unsure whether the revelation notice came in this report or elsewhere.
BAGHAWI:96:9/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : " قال أبو جهل : هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم ؟ فقيل : نعم

BAGHAWI:96:10/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:10/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:10/r1.claim: The passage was revealed about Abu Jahl, who forbade the Prophet from praying.
BAGHAWI:96:10/r1.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل ، نهى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الصلاة

BAGHAWI:96:10/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:10/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI:96:10/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports Abu Jahl’s threat to trample Muhammad while praying, his recoil at an unseen trench of fire and wings, and the Prophet’s statement that angels would seize him; the narrator is unsure whether the revelation notice came in this report or elsewhere.
BAGHAWI:96:10/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : " قال أبو جهل : هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم ؟ فقيل : نعم

BAYDAWI:96:10/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:10/r1.speaker: أبو جهل
BAYDAWI:96:10/r1.claim: The same occasion report recounts Abū Jahl's threat to trample Muhammad during prayer and his retreat after seeing a fiery trench, terror, and wings.
BAYDAWI:96:10/r1.anchor: في أبي جهل ، قال : لو رأيت محمدا ساجدا

BAYDAWI:96:10/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:10/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:10/r2.claim: The indefinite “servant” intensifies the ugliness of forbidding prayer and emphasizes the worshipper's complete servitude.
BAYDAWI:96:10/r2.anchor: في تقبيح النهي ، والدلالة على كمال عبودية المنهي

BIQAI:96:10/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:10/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:10/r1.claim: The indefinite noun intensifies the ugliness of forbidding and signals the worshipper's complete servanthood; preventing a servant from serving his master is especially heinous.
BIQAI:96:10/r1.anchor: معبراً بالعبودية منكراً للمبالغة في تقبيح النهي

BIQAI:96:10/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:10/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:10/r2.claim: Prayer is a servant's connection to his Lord and the greatest worship, joining nearness to God with complete withdrawal from creation; forbidding it withholds a due right through envy or rebellion.

BIQAI:96:10/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:10/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:10/r3.claim: People in every age characteristically oppose those of virtue and obstruct good so that others do not attain perfection.
BIQAI:96:10/r3.anchor: من طبع أهل كل زمان عداوة أهل الفضل

IBNASHUR:96:6/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r5.speaker: بعضهم
IBNASHUR:96:6/r5.claim: Some saw the prayer reference as conflicting with an immediate revelation after the first five verses, since the five daily prayers were prescribed at the later Night Journey; they proposed an intervening revelation or denied this was the first sūra.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r5.anchor: واختلفوا في أن هذه الآيات إلى آخر السورة نزلت عقب الخمس الآيات الماضية وجعلوا مما يناكده ذِكر الصلاة فيها

IBNASHUR:96:6/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r9.speaker: الحربي
IBNASHUR:96:6/r9.claim: Al-Ḥarbī, as quoted by al-Suhaylī, says that before the Night Journey the Prophet prayed once before sunset and once before sunrise.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r9.anchor: ذكر الحربي أن الصلاة قبل الإسراء كانت صلاة قبل غروب الشمس ( أي العصر ) وصلاة قبل طلوعها ( أي الصبح )

IBNASHUR:96:6/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r10.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
IBNASHUR:96:6/r10.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Sallām agrees that the Prophet prayed before sunset and before sunrise; al-Suhaylī also says the Night Journey and obligation of five prayers came a year before the Hijra.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r10.anchor: وقال يحيى بن سلام مثله ،  وقال :  كان الإسراء وفرض الصلوات الخمس قبل الهجرة بعام

IBNASHUR:96:6/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:6/r11.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr identifies the prayer as an unregulated pre-obligation form, distinct from the five daily prayers, that included prostration and was performed publicly where polytheists could see it, provoking Abū Jahl.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r11.anchor: فالوجه أن تكون الصلاة التي كان يصليها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صلاة غير الصلوات الخمس بل كانت هيئة غير مضبوطة بكيفية وفيها سجود

IBNASHUR:96:6/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:6/r12.claim: He holds that the verses through the sūra's end followed a short pause after its opening verses, when the Prophet's prayer and the beginning of revelation became known; adjacent recited verses normally follow in revelation order absent clear contrary proof, and this remains the first-revealed sūra.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r12.anchor: فالوجه أن تكون هذه الآيات إلى بقية السورة قد نزلت بعد فترة قصيرة من نزول أول السورة حدثت فيها صلاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR:96:10/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:10/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:10/r1.claim: Though the episode concerns the Prophet, the generic ʿabd avoids direct address because the wonder lies in forbidding prayer itself, regardless of the worshipper's identity.
IBNASHUR:96:10/r1.anchor: وعدل عن التعبير عنه بضمير الخطاب لأن التعجيب من نفس النهي عن الصلاة بقطع النظر عن خصوصية المصلّي

IBNASHUR:96:10/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:10/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:10/r2.claim: The imperfect yanhā vividly presents the past event, and the prohibited act is omitted because it is understood from the prayer context.
IBNASHUR:96:10/r2.anchor: وصيغة المضارع في قوله :  { ينهى } لاستحضار الحالة العجيبة وإلا فإن نهيه قد مضى .  والمنهي عنه محذوف

IBNASHUR:96:14/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:14/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:14/r6.claim: The pronouns in kadhdhaba and tawallā refer to the prohibitor in verses 9–10; context directs pronouns to their different antecedents, and the object of kadhdhaba is omitted because it is understood as the praying servant.
IBNASHUR:96:14/r6.anchor: وضمير { كذب وتولى } عائد إلى { الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } [ العلق :  9 ،  10 ]

IBNATIYYA:96:8/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:8/r4.speaker: المفسرين
IBNATIYYA:96:8/r4.claim: The commentators unanimously identify the one who forbids as Abu Jahl and the praying servant as Muhammad.
IBNATIYYA:96:8/r4.anchor: ولم يختلف أحد من المفسرين في أن الناهي : أبو جهل ، وأن العبد المصلي محمد

IBNATIYYA:96:10/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:10/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:10/r1.claim: Arayta is an interrogative challenge and, unlike knowledge-based vision, does not take two objects.
IBNATIYYA:96:10/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { أرأيت } توقيف ، وهو فعل لا يتعدى إلى مفعولين على حد الرؤية

IBNKATHIR:96:9/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:9/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:9/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr says the passage was revealed about Abū Jahl, who threatened the Prophet for praying at the House.
IBNKATHIR:96:9/r1.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل ، لعنه الله ، توعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR:96:9/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:9/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:9/r2.claim: God first admonishes the forbidding man in the gentlest manner.
IBNKATHIR:96:9/r2.anchor: فوعظه الله تعالى بالتي هي أحسن أولا

IBNKATHIR:96:10/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:10/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:10/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr says the passage was revealed about Abū Jahl, who threatened the Prophet for praying at the House.
IBNKATHIR:96:10/r1.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل ، لعنه الله ، توعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR:96:10/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:10/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:10/r2.claim: God first admonishes the forbidding man in the gentlest manner.
IBNKATHIR:96:10/r2.anchor: فوعظه الله تعالى بالتي هي أحسن أولا

IBNKATHIR:96:11/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:11/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:11/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir says the passage was revealed about Abu Jahl, who threatened the Prophet for praying at the House.
IBNKATHIR:96:11/r1.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل ، لعنه الله ، توعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على الصلاة عند البيت

IBNKATHIR:96:12/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:12/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:12/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir says the passage was revealed about Abu Jahl, who threatened the Prophet for praying at the House.
IBNKATHIR:96:12/r1.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل ، لعنه الله ، توعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على الصلاة عند البيت

IBNKATHIR:96:14/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:14/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:14/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir says the passage was revealed about Abu Jahl, who threatened the Prophet for praying at the House.
IBNKATHIR:96:14/r1.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل ، لعنه الله ، توعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على الصلاة عند البيت

MUSNAD-AHMAD:3044/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3044/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3044/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl tried to stop Muhammad praying and boasted of his council; al-ʿAlaq 96:10–13 was revealed, and Ibn Abbas says angels would seize him if he summoned them.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3044/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " جاء أبو جهل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI:96:9/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:9/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:9/r1.claim: The passage was revealed about Abu Jahl. Abu Hurayra reports that he vowed by al-Lat and al-ʿUzza to trample Muhammad's neck and soil his face, then approached him in prayer but recoiled; he said a trench of fire, terror, and wings stood between them.
MAWARDI:96:9/r1.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل ، روى أبو هريرة أن أبا جهل قال : واللات والعزّى لئن رأيت محمداً

MAWARDI:96:9/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:9/r2.speaker: النبي
MAWARDI:96:9/r2.claim: The Prophet said that if Abu Jahl came near, angels would seize him limb by limb; al-Tirmidhi grades this report hasan sahih gharib.
MAWARDI:96:9/r2.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : " لو دنا مني لاختطفته الملائكة

MAWARDI:96:9/r3.author: al-Māwardī

NASAFI:96:10/r1.anchor: أي : أرأيت أبا جهل ينهى محمداً عن الصلاة

QURTUBI:96:9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:9/r1.claim: The one who forbids is Abu Jahl, and the servant he forbids is Muhammad; Abu Hurayra reports Abu Jahl threatened to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him praying, prompting these verses in astonishment.
QURTUBI:96:9/r1.anchor: وهو أبو جهل " عبدا " وهو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم . فإن أبا جهل قال
